measures.title: Sale or Lease of City Property Containing Recreational Ballfields Must Be Approved by Referendum Vote
measures.summary: Adds a provision to the Stuart City Charter barring the City Commission from selling, conveying or leasing for more than one year (including renewal options) any city-owned real property containing recreational ballfields unless voters first approve it in a public referendum. The referendum would follow the charter's Section 9.04 procedures used for vacating public streets or abandoning right-of-way.
measures.yesMeans: The charter will require voter approval before the city sells or leases for more than a year any city property containing recreational ballfields.
measures.noMeans: The charter is not changed, and no referendum is required for such sales or leases.

measures.title: Rescind Prior Referendum Requiring Commercial Leasing of Parcel Adjoining City Property Fronting Tidally Influenced Waters
measures.summary: Asks whether the city should rescind the November 8, 2011, referendum requirement to lease an undeveloped 1.97-acre commercial parcel fronting US-1 opposite North River Shores Boulevard, whose lease was to fund maintenance of the Haney Creek Preserve. If rescinded, the parcel may be converted to conservation and added to the Haney Creek Preserve.
measures.yesMeans: The 2011 leasing requirement is rescinded, so the 1.97-acre parcel may be added to the Haney Creek Preserve as conservation land.
measures.noMeans: The 2011 requirement to lease the parcel commercially stays in place.
